scope: Current full-graph resident-native execution: unchanged compact CPU inner, device-resident joint state and DOP853 workspace, native monitor/evaluator and native observation-delay queue, CPU discrete patches and complete checkpoint export. Independent numerical QA only; not physiology, fitting, solver changes or background qualification.
approval_scope: The architecture and prospective numerical gate are approved for low-load implementation. This document is not a runtime-test authorization, numerical-pass claim, performance result or production-backend approval.

solver_required.input_interpolation: Unchanged original input contract for each bound channel; bind the complete actual interpolation/breakpoint/left-right-limit identity before execution. No substitution of the old small-fixture analytic contract.

scenario_required.output_scope: Current unchanged owner cohort and full dependency closure, retaining the 8.31 degree output range. This cohort does not establish coverage of every research RGC class.
scenario_required.binding_before_execution: Freeze source/graph/owner/order/weights/parameters/solver/channel/reference-state/checkpoint-layout and complete aux hashes; attach this contract hash. Unknown or mismatched identity stops evaluation. Do not weaken old checkpoint backend-identity rejection to import the QA state.

scale_definition: S_i=max(abs(frozen reference QA initial state_i), existing unit_registry.scale_floor); never rescale from subsequent drift or candidate values
roundoff_scope_limit: 8192eps remains the previously allocated engineering screen, not a certified rounding bound for large native reductions or a global-error guarantee. No increase is permitted after observing results. An unsupported arithmetic/monitor quantity or an unproved budget propagation is inconclusive and blocks adoption; it does not inherit a new arbitrary allowance.
solver_execution: Preserve each original interval boundary and controller restart, both initial-step RHS evaluations, original coefficients and expression order, full-state RMS dimension including held states, acceptance/rejection and dense polynomial/endpoint choice. Keep original reductions in the initial resident implementation. Accepted/rejected schedules must match in the first QA gate; otherwise stop even if the final state happens to be close.

outputs.V_gE_gI_release_native_readouts: Same typed B formula with scale frozen from the reference initial output; require an existing registered unit/floor and preserve every declared port validation
outputs.conditional_rate_Hz: alpha/beta * B_voltage + 8192eps*max(abs(reference_rate),1Hz); strict-past history must match exactly
outputs.event_time: For identical uniform u and unchanged history, use the original event-time formula and the interval from lambda_ref +/- declared rate allowance. Same cell/order/bin; no shifts/resampling. An actual event with nonpositive lower rate is inconclusive, not accepted.
outputs.delay_values: Use the original port's typed output allowance, preserving timestamp brackets, prehistory, interpolation arithmetic order, prune rule and retained rows. No sampled or reduced queue substitutes for the full numerical payload.

monitor.coverage: Every original state/port/domain/gap/history/discrete-one-step-defect check at every original callback, with unchanged numerical thresholds, observation count, complete-window criterion and qualification duration
monitor.storage: Preserve per-cell lo/hi/max_abs_rhs/defect and immutable reference den; compute original normalized per-cell criteria before reducing. Preserve state/criterion traversal and first-argmax tie rules.
monitor.exact_fields: Report schema, observation stamps/count/coverage, failure labels, history/gap decisions and pass/fail must match exactly
monitor.numeric_fields: Save both full raw reports and per-cell statistic differences. Excursion bounds follow corresponding lo/hi state budgets; RHS norm bounds follow width*RHS_allowance/den. Discrete-defect bounds use the separately required direct transition-output witness below. Other derived-statistic bounds require explicit pre-evaluation typed propagation; missing propagation is inconclusive, never a guessed global norm tolerance. Near-threshold intervals that cannot guarantee the same original decision stop evaluation.
monitor.discrete_transition_witness: At every original monitor point, evaluate each original pure one-step transition in both arms from their respective same-time pre-transition state and original input/sampling context, without committing it or consuming RNG. Preserve both transition outputs as independent QA observables and require abs(transition_candidate_i-transition_reference_i)<=B_transition_i with B_transition_i=B_i, using the same original state unit, frozen initial S_i and unchanged state budget formula. The current-state comparison must independently satisfy abs(state_candidate_i-state_reference_i)<=B_state_i=B_i. Missing either witness is inconclusive and blocks adoption; do not estimate nonlinear propagation instead.
monitor.discrete_defect_allowance: For defect_i=abs(transition_i-state_i)/period, the direct witnessed bound is (B_transition_i+B_state_i)/period. The corresponding original normalized monitor bound is width*(B_transition_i+B_state_i)/(period*den_i); per-cell temporal maxima preserve this bound. Keep original positive period, frozen den_i, exact callback alignment and expression order. Preserve numeric witnesses and do not turn the bound into a new background pass/fail threshold.
monitor.dominant: Retain both dominant state/cell/criterion witnesses. Near-equal maxima may select different cells only when original first-argmax semantics and already-declared numeric bounds explain the difference; otherwise stop.
monitor.failure_timing: No delayed checks across original failure barriers; merging device predicates within one logical stage cannot postpone rejection to frame/window/batch completion

discrete_aux: Grid origin, component_tick_indices, sample_index, counts/history, PCG64 state, draw order/count, delay timestamps, pending-event cell/order/bin identity and input phase exact. Record u, both probabilities, declared allowance and margin. A changed event decision or uniform inside the uncertainty interval stops the run without extra draws or resampling.
event_order: Common pre-transition sampling snapshot -> compute all due BC/rod transitions -> commit state -> increment due component tick indices -> original RGC sample_spikes updates aux/RNG -> increment sample_index. Rod author interval-start input and old-state update order unchanged.
resident_ownership: Only explicit current-generation inner patches may modify resident state. No stale event/monitor evidence across state/input/left-right-limit/sampling/due-set/history/delay/parameter/graph generations. No aliasing of returned samples/final snapshots with reusable RK workspaces. Functional advance must not mutate its supplied reference state.
checkpoint: Explicit runtime export materializes complete same-generation state, native observation queue, input position, clocks/history/PCG64/pending events and runtime identity. The background reference binding, monitor report and qualification metadata remain the responsibility of the existing outer BackgroundCheckpointStore envelope; plain RetinaState export alone does not contain or establish that qualification. Full checkpoint publication requires the outer-store integration and all existing strict loading/hash/qualification checks. Until that integration is implemented and verified, do not claim full qualified checkpoint support. Storage residency does not confer background qualification.
invalid_inputs: No tolerance for NaN/Inf, negative native domain/light, invalid channel/layout/unit identity or missing state; preserve original rejection and failure timing, with no clipping
QA_initial_state: Identical complete real-graph diagnostic initial state and aux in both arms. Preserve reference scales and all original initial values; do not move RGC V to mu or alter physiology/parameters to manufacture a performance event. A short diagnostic window remains NOT_FIT_ELIGIBLE.
QA_scenario: One prospectively bound 8-10ms representative scenario with a short background portion and time-varying input spanning at least one actual 150fps frame boundary, original 100us rod and 1ms BC/RGC clocks, left/right limits, all original observations and at least one actual dense request. Freeze exact inputs/timestamps before execution. No long warmup or fitting. Report missing spike coverage explicitly; old 52-spike small-fixture evidence is not a real-graph pass.
validation_status: No runtime evaluation, CUDA initialization, JIT, simulation, benchmark or numerical QA has been performed for this contract. Static source/JSON validation cannot satisfy it.
execution_hold: During the user's gaming restriction, all simulations, benchmarks, graph assembly, large-array loading, CUDA/JIT and heavy checks remain prohibited. Runtime work requires the user's later explicit authorization; never schedule an automatic timed start or move it to another computer.
stopping: Any numeric/aux/domain/coverage/qualification/failure-timing gate failure, unsupported budget propagation, changed accept/reject schedule or uncertain event/threshold decision stops adoption. Keep failure evidence; no post-result threshold adjustment, hidden numerical changes or automatic retry matrix.
performance_gate: Only after authorized correctness validation: compare complete identical-observer/input/event/output E2E, separate cold costs and extra QA readback. At least 20 percent lower hot wall time is the prospective engineering-value gate, not a prediction. A slower candidate stops; at most one additional paired run if noise or the threshold is unclear. Existing memory/STOP guards remain. Future proposed run budget: 15 minutes total including one assembly and at most 3 minutes in testing, subject to explicit authorization.
excluded: GPU-inner/fused-inner continuation, controller persistence across event intervals, changed integration algorithm/precision/tolerances/norm dimension, relaxed monitoring/background qualification, graph/cell/feedback/range approximation, default-backend switch or automatic production deployment
relationship_to_old_contract: Independent new full-graph resident-native scope. compact_device_fp64_v2.json and its hashes/results remain unchanged and are not automatically applicable. This contract preserves its existing allocation fractions rather than claiming that the old small-graph validation proved the new scope.
